signals.signal: H1-2026 record net profit attributable to shareholders EUR 617mn (EPS EUR 0.47, RoaTBV normalised 15.7%; Q2 alone EUR 336mn, +22% yoy). FY-2026 targets formally UPGRADED at the 29/07/2026 release: EPS ~EUR 0.90, NII EUR 2.0bn (from EUR 1.9bn), RoaTBV ~15%, C:I <35%, CET1 >13%, performing loans >EUR 40bn. Loans EUR 39.0bn (+9% yoy), deposits EUR 68.4bn, LDR 65%.
signals.source_name: Piraeus Financial Holdings — H1 2026 Financial Results Press Release (PDF)
signals.implies: Self-funded capex capacity is rising, not constrained: a bank raising guidance mid-year and running a 31% Q2 cost/income has both the money and the efficiency mandate to buy automation. This is the budget pool behind every other Piraeus signal below — ATM/self-service refresh, cash automation, managed services.
signals.likelihood: Very likely to keep spending; FY-2026 budget already committed
signals.followup: Ask IR/Group COO office for the 2026-27 technology capex split by channel (branch, ATM/self-service, payments) at the Q3-2026 release (late Oct 2026).

signals.signal: Domestic branch network FLAT at 368 branches at both Jun.25 and Jun.26; Group branches flat at 384 across 30/06/2025, 31/12/2025, 31/03/2026 and 30/06/2026. Domestic FTEs UP from 7.4k to 8.1k (Group employees 7,726 -> 8,518), including c.700 FTEs from Ethniki Insurance.
signals.source_name: Piraeus — H1 2026 Financial Results Presentation (PDF), slides 13 and 6 KPI table
signals.implies: Greece's #1 retail bank has STOPPED shrinking its branch estate — the same pattern flagged in Romania (CEC Bank). Efficiency has to come from automating inside a retained network, which is exactly the cash-recycler / in-branch kiosk / teller-automation case. Sell automation-in-place, not consolidation.
signals.likelihood: High — network stable through at least FY-2026 plan horizon (370 branches in the 2026-30 strategic plan)
signals.followup: Model a recycler/teller-automation business case for 368 domestic branches; benchmark against the Czech shared-network branch-cash-desk census in the baseline.

signals.signal: Fleet stated as 1,500 ATMs at Jun.26 (deck slide 26 and ESG slide: 'c.370 branches, c.1,500 ATMs'), and 1,500 ATMs in the 5 March 2026 Capital Markets Day deck. This is ABOVE the 1,300 units Piraeus itself said it retained in July 2025 after transferring its off-site machines to Cashflex — implying roughly +200 machines of net re-expansion of the on-us estate in ~12 months.
signals.source_name: Piraeus — H1 2026 Results Presentation (PDF) slide 26; cross-checked vs Piraeus statement reported by Insider.gr
signals.implies: Direct ATM/self-service hardware, software and managed-services opportunity. A fleet that grew back after an off-site disposal means the bank decided on-us ATMs are strategic again — and a ~200-machine delta is a procurement event that has already happened or is happening now. Also a deposit-automation white-space question: Piraeus discloses no deposit-capable/recycler split.
signals.likelihood: Likely — refresh cycle plus re-expansion active now
signals.followup: Establish the deposit-capable/recycling share of the 1,500 (not disclosed anywhere); pull the piraeusbank.gr branch/ATM locator and count deposit-enabled sites, and ask who supplied the ~200 added machines.

signals.signal: Explicit ATM and branch self-service workstream disclosed under the Transformation Programme: 'At ATMs, enhancements to cash management and the user interface improve availability and operational efficiency'; deck lists 'Optimised ATM cash replenishment to improve cash availability' and 'Refined ATM screen content'; online appointment booking now runs through branch information KIOSKS without e-banking credentials.
signals.source_name: Piraeus — H1 2026 Press Release, 'Transformation Programme Developments in the first half of 2026'; H1 2026 Presentation slide 22
signals.implies: Named, funded, in-flight projects that map 1:1 onto Printec's cash-forecasting/cash-cycle optimisation software, ATM multivendor application/screen layer, in-branch kiosks and managed services. 'Optimised cash replenishment' in plain terms = predicting how much money each machine needs so it neither runs dry nor sits on idle cash — a standard cash-management-software sale.
signals.followup: Approach the Group COO / Channels team with a cash-cycle optimisation and multivendor-application reference; ask whether replenishment optimisation is in-house or vendor-supplied.

signals.signal: Capital Markets Day (London, 05/03/2026) Strategic Plan 2026-2030: CapEx 2026-2030 of ~EUR 800mn of which ~80% is for AI/technology (i.e. ~EUR 640mn), plus ~EUR 50mn CapEx for Ethniki Insurance transformation. Targets ~EUR 70mn of efficiencies from AI and technology, 15% of existing capacity to be unlocked, C:I ~30% average 2026-30, RoaTBV ~18% by 2030, ~EUR 5bn total distributions.
signals.source_name: Piraeus — Capital Markets Day 2026, Strategic Plan 2026-2030 Presentation (PDF)
signals.implies: A named, board-approved ~EUR 640mn five-year technology wallet in a single 17-country-footprint market. Everything Printec sells that carries software and managed services — ATM/self-service estate, cash automation, eKYC, transaction monitoring, HSM — competes for a slice of this. Anchor all Greek account planning on this number.
signals.followup: Obtain the CMD IR Toolkit XLSX (Strategic-Plan-IRToolkit-2026.xlsx) for the year-by-year capex phasing; map Printec offer lines to the five strategic pillars (pillar 4 is 'AI and technology').

signals.signal: IT CapEx step-up disclosed on the efficiency slide: ~EUR 140mn average per year for 2024-2026 versus ~EUR 100mn average per year for 2022-2023. Depreciation rising 'on the back of CapEx IT spending'; H1.26 total OpEx EUR 453mn with C:I 34% H1 / 31% Q2.
signals.source_name: Piraeus — H1 2026 Financial Results Presentation (PDF), slide 13 'Investing for growth while maintaining best-in-class efficiency'
signals.implies: A ~40% step-up in annual IT capex that is already running, not promised. Confirms the CMD wallet is being spent. Sizes the realistic annual addressable pool for a hardware+software+managed-services vendor in Greece.
signals.followup: Verify the exact label-to-value mapping of the two IT CapEx bars against the IR factsheet XLSX (IRTool-Website_H1_2026.xlsx) before quoting the figures externally.

signals.signal: 'Newra' AI Hub — announced 20/04/2026 as a Piraeus + Accenture AI hub powered by Anthropic (operating under Accenture's Anthropic Business Group and its Data & AI Center of Excellence in Athens), formally named 10/07/2026. Set up as a permanent innovation and delivery engine with active recruitment of specialised AI talent. H1-2026 disclosure: ~90 AI use cases in development, 20 business AI use cases live in production, >100 internal use cases catalogued, 99% AI adoption across licensed users, ~615k e-banking virtual-assistant questions in H1 (+21% vs 2025), target 'AI-native bank by 2030'.
signals.source_name: Piraeus Group press releases 20/04/2026 and 10/07/2026; H1 2026 Presentation slide 20
signals.implies: Accenture has taken the strategic AI-delivery seat at Greece's largest bank. For Printec this is both a threat (a global SI now sits between the bank and its process/channel roadmap) and an opening: Newra redesigns processes but does not supply devices, cash logistics, HSMs or transaction-monitoring engines. Position as the execution layer under Newra's designs, especially where AI touches cash forecasting, fraud/AML scoring and eKYC.
signals.likelihood: Certain — hub is operational and hiring
signals.followup: Map Newra's 20 live use cases; find which ones need device-level or payment-rail integration and get Printec named as the delivery partner for those.

signals.signal: First Greek bank certified to ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems) — certified by TUV NORD Hellas S.A., award ceremony 30/06/2026, certificate valid three years effective 01/04/2026. Scope covers the Group AI governance framework plus two production applications (customer Digital Assistant on e-banking/mobile, and the internal Employee Assistant on platform 'Yello'). Explicitly framed as EU AI Act readiness.
signals.source_name: Oikonomikos Taxydromos (ot.gr) report of the Piraeus/TUV NORD Hellas certification
signals.implies: Piraeus has set a governance bar that any AI-bearing supplier will now be measured against — including AML/transaction-monitoring and fraud engines, which are high-risk systems under the EU AI Act. Printec bids into Greek banks should carry documented model governance, explainability and AI Act mapping as a qualification requirement, not a differentiator.
signals.likelihood: Certification in force to 2029; peer banks likely to follow
signals.followup: Confirm on the Piraeus corporate site (primary) and check whether supplier AI-governance evidence has entered Piraeus procurement templates.

signals.signal: Piraeus raised its Snappi holding from 55% to 56.28% in Q1-2026 (EUR 10mn cash SCI), then bought a further 11.72% for EUR 41mn in Q2-2026 taking it to 68%, and injected a further EUR 7mn of a EUR 10mn SCI keeping 68%. Snappi users grew 9k (Jun.25) -> 60k (Dec.25) -> 100k (Mar.26) -> >210k app users (Jun.26), with ~135k onboarded customers, >70 merchants onboarded for Snappi Pay Later, >15 brand partnerships (Shell, OASA, Sky Express, Domino's, Vodafone CU, Public, AB, Freenow, Blue Star Ferries, Fast Pass Tolls, efood), a savings account at up to 2.25% and 'Cash Now' instant interest-free loans up to EUR 1,000. Branchless, ECB-licensed, low-capex, explicitly built for embedded finance and BaaS.
signals.source_name: Piraeus H1 2026 Interim Financial Report (Greek, ATHEX/Euronext filing), note 26; H1 2026 Presentation slide 23
signals.implies: A 2.3x user jump in six months on a branchless bank = pure digital-onboarding/eKYC and real-time fraud/transaction-monitoring volume, with no branch fallback. The EUR 41mn paid for 11.72% implies a c.EUR 350mn valuation, so the parent is doubling down. Snappi's BNPL merchant network (>70 merchants) is also a POS/acquiring and merchant-onboarding KYB surface.
signals.likelihood: High — scaling through 2026-27, BaaS model stated
signals.followup: Identify Snappi's current eKYC/liveness and transaction-monitoring vendors and its BNPL merchant-onboarding stack; a fast-scaling neobank typically re-tenders these at the 250-500k user mark.

signals.signal: Cashflex's own public ATM locator API (https://cashflex.gr/wp-json/atm/v1/all) returned 480 ATM sites when pulled on 27/08/2026 — materially below the ~820-850 off-site machines Piraeus transferred to Cashflex in July 2025. Piraeus's H1-2026 interim report confirms 'Cashflex Leitourgia kai diacheirisi diktyon ATM A.E. (formerly KEA ATM)', business object 'development and operation of an ATM network', is accounted for as an ASSOCIATE over which the Group exercises significant influence despite holding under 20%. The Cashflex newsroom's most recent item is dated 01/10/2025 — no 2026 network update published.
signals.source_name: Cashflex public ATM locator JSON API (own site) + Piraeus H1 2026 Interim Financial Report, associates schedule
signals.implies: Printec's own Greek off-site ATM venture: the publicly discoverable estate is roughly 40% smaller than the transferred fleet, which is either estate rationalisation after the August-2025 fee law or an incomplete locator. Either way this is a number Printec should reconcile internally before it appears in a competitor's pitch — and a changed count is itself the recurring signal to track.
signals.likelihood: Locator is live and machine-readable; re-pull each run
signals.followup: INTERNAL: reconcile the 480 published sites against Cashflex's actual installed base; if the locator under-reports, fix it — it is the number outsiders will quote. Re-pull the API every run and log the delta.

signals.entity: Piraeus Financial Holdings / Greek off-site ATM market
signals.signal: Greek law (amendment to L.5167/2024, in force 11/08/2025) zeroed DIAS interbank withdrawal fees, abolished own-bank ATM withdrawal charges, capped third-party/independent ATM withdrawals at EUR 1.50, made balance enquiries free everywhere, made withdrawals free at the single ATM in a one-ATM municipality, and made third-party withdrawals FREE where there is a direct or indirect shareholding link between the ATM operator and the customer's bank. Piraeus separately cut its own out-of-network withdrawal charge from EUR 0.60 to EUR 0.50.
signals.source_name: ProtoThema English (national daily) report on the fee regime in force; Piraeus statement reported by Insider.gr
signals.implies: The shareholding-link clause hits the Piraeus/Cashflex structure directly: Piraeus cardholders withdraw free at Cashflex machines, so the venture's revenue per transaction collapses on its largest likely user base. Independent-ATM-deployer economics in Greece now depend on volume, uptime and cost-per-replenishment rather than fee level — which pushes value toward cash-cycle optimisation, remote monitoring and managed services (Printec's own margin lever in its own JV).
signals.followup: Locate the actual ministerial decision / gazette text (FEK) for the L.5167/2024 amendment rather than press summaries, and check for any 2026 amendment; log the FEK reference for the file.

signals.signal: Selected by the Eurosystem on 14/07/2026 as one of 36 payment service providers for the digital euro pilot, responding to a call for interest published March 2026. Piraeus will act as a PSP in cooperation with the Bank of Greece. Pilot starts in H2-2027 and runs 12 months.
signals.implies: A dated, multi-year integration programme with hard downstream requirements: digital-euro wallets, offline/holding-limit handling, key management and secure element provisioning (HSM), plus acceptance at POS and — crucially for Printec — cash-in/cash-out at ATMs, which the ECB scheme expects banks to support. Design and vendor selection work happens 2026-H1 2027, i.e. NOW.
signals.followup: Confirm against the ECB/Eurosystem primary announcement of 14/07/2026 and the published list of 36 PSPs; identify which Greek entities are on it and open a digital-euro ATM cash-in/out and HSM conversation before the H1-2027 build window.

signals.signal: H1-2026 digital KPIs: digital customer onboarding 23% (+1.9ppts vs 2025); digital sales penetration 31% (+6.7ppts vs 2025, and 27% at CMD vs 19% two years earlier); mobile active users +12%; transactions on mobile +15%; SELF-SERVICE ACTIONS +11% in H1.26 vs 2025 (+17% yoy at the March CMD); 97% three-month retention; 3.2mn digital clients of 4.5mn total. Against that, disclosed average e-banking online-transacting clients slipped from 1,120k (Dec.25) to 1,066k (Mar.26) to 1,049k (Jun.26).
signals.source_name: Piraeus — H1 2026 Financial Results Presentation (PDF) slide 19; CMD 2026 Presentation; H1 2026 Press Release KPI table
signals.implies: Digital onboarding at only 23% means roughly three in four new customers are still opened through an assisted channel — a large, quantified eKYC/remote-identification gap at the country's biggest bank. Rising self-service actions with a flat branch estate is the classic recycler/kiosk demand curve. The e-banking transacting-client dip is worth watching: it suggests channel migration into the app rather than growth in overall digital reach.
signals.likelihood: Onboarding target improving but gap persists into 2027
signals.followup: Pitch digital onboarding/eKYC against the 23% figure explicitly; ask whether the constraint is regulatory (remote identification rules) or technical.

signals.signal: S&P Global Ratings upgraded Piraeus on 20/07/2026 to investment grade, long- and short-term issuer credit ratings to 'BBB-/A-3' from 'BB+/B', stable outlook — completing full investment-grade status across all major agencies. Separately, in June 2026 Piraeus completed the Ermis IX synthetic securitisation of a ~EUR 1.0bn shipping portfolio (RWA relief ~EUR 640mn, capital relief ~EUR 84mn, SRT approval obtained), and is accruing EUR 650mn of cash distribution out of 2026 profit.
signals.source_name: Piraeus — H1 2026 Financial Results Press Release (PDF)
signals.implies: Cheaper wholesale funding plus released capital removes the classic Greek-bank objection to multi-year technology and equipment commitments. Useful as a financing-terms argument in any managed-services or ATM-as-a-service proposal, where the bank can now compare opex-vs-capex on genuinely investment-grade funding costs.
signals.followup: Fetch the S&P research update of 20/07/2026 itself for the supervisory/technology commentary if a licensed seat is available.

signals.signal: Beyond-banking build-out disclosed for H1-2026: 'Farmclick' agri-supplies B2B/B2C marketplace launched May 2026 and now rolling out commercially nationwide (held as associate 'FarmClick powered by Piraeus and Wikifarmer A.E.'); the first fully digital, AI-powered end-to-end mortgage platform in the Greek market running in PILOT mode (application to disbursement); and the 'Piraeus Youth' family-banking app in development for teenagers/Gen Z with parental supervision of a family account.
signals.source_name: Piraeus — H1 2026 Financial Results Press Release, Business Developments section; H1 2026 Interim Financial Report associates schedule
signals.implies: Three new customer-acquisition surfaces, each of which needs identity proofing, minor/guardian verification and payment-instrument issuance outside the branch — squarely digital onboarding/eKYC plus transaction monitoring. A youth/family product in particular forces age-verification and parental-consent flows that Greek banks have not built at scale before.
signals.likelihood: Mortgage platform exits pilot in FY-2026/H1-2027; Youth app on plan
signals.followup: Track the digital mortgage platform's move from pilot to production (likely announced at Q3-2026 or FY-2026 results) — that is the eKYC/e-signature procurement trigger.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed for 2026-08-27). PRIMARY-FIRST: opened and text-extracted the actual PDFs — H1-2026 Results Presentation (71pp, 29/07/2026), H1-2026 Press Release (25pp), the Capital Markets Day 2026 Strategic Plan deck (66pp, 05/03/2026), and the Greek H1-2026 Interim Financial Report filed on ATHEX/Euronext (671k chars) — rather than relying on summaries. Also pulled Piraeus's own IR indexes, the Capital Markets Day materials page, two Piraeus press releases (20/04/2026 Accenture/Anthropic AI hub, 10/07/2026 Newra naming), and Cashflex's own site and its undocumented locator JSON API. Angles varied deliberately vs the last run: (1) issuer IR PDFs, (2) the ATHEX/Euronext OAM filing in Greek, (3) a vendor-JV locator API, (4) Greek-language financial press for the ATM fee-law and digital-euro items, (5) the Workable ATS jobs API. NEW/CHANGED vs 30/07/2026 baseline: FY-2026 guidance upgrade (NII 1.9->2.0bn, CET1 >13%); Snappi 55%->68% with EUR 41mn paid for 11.72% and users 100k->210k in one quarter; Newra AI hub named 10/07/2026; ISO/IEC 42001 first in Greece; digital-euro PSP selection 14/07/2026; S&P full IG 20/07/2026; the 1,500 vs 1,300 ATM-count tension; and a fresh 480-site Cashflex locator count. RECONCILIATION performed as instructed: group-level disclosure (1,500 ATMs / 368 domestic branches, Jun-26) checked against the July-2025 country-level statements (1,300 retained + ~820-850 to Cashflex) — they do NOT reconcile, and that gap is reported as a signal rather than smoothed over. GENUINE GAPS: (a) Piraeus discloses no deposit-capable/recycler split of its 1,500 ATMs anywhere in the H1 deck, press release, interim report or CMD deck, and its store locator sits behind a redirecting API that did not yield a machine-readable feed on this pass — so the Greek recycler white space remains unquantified, unlike Bulgaria/Croatia in the baseline; (b) no vendor is named for Piraeus ATM hardware or cash-management software in any 2026 disclosure; (c) the Cashflex 2026 network size is not published by Cashflex itself (newsroom stale since 01/10/2025), so the 480 locator count is the only current number; (d) Piraeus is a private issuer so Greek public-procurement registers (KIMDIS/Diavgeia/TED) carry no Piraeus tenders — no tender deadlines exist for this unit this window, which is why every deadline field is empty; (e) the Workable ATS account 'piraeus-bank' returned only 5 open roles with no channel/cash/AML titles, so no early-intent hiring signal.

Two Piraeus PDF paths 404'd before the correct ones were found: .../H1/1_26_Financial_Results_Presentation.pdf (404, the URL as surfaced by search) and .../H1/H1_2026_Press_Release.pdf (404) — the working paths are H1_2026_Financial_Results_Presentation.pdf and Q2_2026-Press-Release.pdf?sc_lang=en, both confirmed 200. piraeusbank.gr store-locator paths /en/idiwtes/store-locator and /el/idiwtes/store-locator returned 404 and /api/storelocator/search returned a 302 to an extranet auth handler — the ATM locator was NOT obtained; logged, not silently dropped.
